hero.subtitle: The unified specification of HTTP semantics for all protocol versions

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 9110 defines the semantics of HTTP that are shared across all versions of the protocol (HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3). It replaces the semantics portions of RFC 7230-7235, providing a single authoritative reference.

By separating semantics from wire format, RFC 9110 makes it clear that GET, POST, 200 OK, and Content-Type mean the same thing regardless of whether the message travels over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, or HTTP/3.

sections.title: Resources
sections.content:
HTTP is a protocol for interacting with resources, which are identified by URIs:

Resource
Any information that can be named by a URI. A resource may be a document, an image, a service endpoint, or any abstract concept.
Representation
The current or intended state of a resource, encoded for transfer. A resource may have multiple representations (HTML, JSON, XML) selected via content negotiation.
URI
A Uniform Resource Identifier provides the address and name for a resource: https://example.com/api/items/42

sections.title: Methods
sections.content:
HTTP methods indicate the desired action to be performed on a resource:

GETRetrieve a representation of the target resource
HEADSame as GET but without the response body
POSTProcess the enclosed representation
PUTReplace the target resource
DELETERemove the target resource
PATCHApply partial modifications
OPTIONSDescribe communication options
CONNECTEstablish a tunnel to the server

sections.title: Status Codes
sections.content:
HTTP status codes communicate the result of the server's attempt to satisfy the request:

200 OKThe request succeeded
201 CreatedA new resource was created
204 No ContentSuccessful but no body to return
301 Moved PermanentlyResource has a new permanent URI
304 Not ModifiedConditional request; cached version is current
400 Bad RequestMalformed request syntax
401 UnauthorizedAuthentication required
403 ForbiddenServer refuses to authorize the request
404 Not FoundResource not found
500 Internal Server ErrorUnexpected server error

sections.title: Content
sections.content:
HTTP messages carry content (previously called "entity body") that represents the state of a resource:

Content-Type
Indicates the media type of the content: Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length
The size of the content in bytes. Required when the message body has a fixed, known length.
Content-Encoding
Compression applied to the content: Content-Encoding: gzip. Applied before transfer encoding.
Content-Language
The natural language(s) of the intended audience: Content-Language: en-US

sections.title: Conditional Requests
sections.content:
Conditional requests allow clients to make requests that only succeed if certain conditions are met, enabling efficient caching and safe concurrent updates:

If-MatchProceed only if the resource's ETag matches (for safe updates)
If-None-MatchProceed only if the resource's ETag does NOT match (for caching)
If-Modified-SinceProceed only if the resource changed after a given date
If-Unmodified-SinceProceed only if the resource has NOT changed since a date
ETagAn opaque validator for a specific version of a resource

ETags enable optimistic concurrency control: a client can PUT an update with If-Match to ensure it doesn't overwrite changes made by another client since the resource was last fetched.
